cuts.title: Lean for biology · two-minute science cut

scenes.narration: Lean for biology: mathematical claims, explicit assumptions, machine-checkable consequences.
scenes.headline: Lean for biology

scenes.narration: Formalized knowledge enables reusable constraints, compatible models, candidate designs and experiments aimed at missing evidence.
scenes.headline: Formal claims make knowledge reusable

scenes.narration: Our test case asks whether zebrafish-inspired fin designs could glide. Published fin-growth genetics and flying-fish measurements frame it.
scenes.headline: A demanding test case: a flying fish

scenes.narration: Lean compiled a fin-beam stiffness bound and rejected a corrupted law. Two computations reused a versioned mechanics claim; independent review kept numerical checks alongside biological questions.
scenes.headline: A conditional theorem, compiled and tested

scenes.narration: The studio links sequence candidates, bioelectricity, mechanics, aerodynamics and collective behavior. Equations, controls, evidence and virtual instruments expose model predictions, not measurements.
scenes.headline: Virtual instruments across scales

scenes.narration: The biological compiler aims to output candidate DNA, a build plan and validation strategy. Today it checks linked artifacts and exposes missing interfaces.
scenes.headline: A biological compiler is an intended output

scenes.narration: Like AlphaFold predictions, candidates need testing. Formal checks, numerical controls and observations turn failures into targeted experiments.
scenes.headline: Predictions need tests

scenes.narration: MCP lets people and agents contribute, challenge and reuse exact work. The flying fish is one test of a shared, checkable foundation for engineering biology.
scenes.headline: Build a shared, checkable foundation
